- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for sentiment-driven support.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% in next 5–7 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If model forecast mean is significantly below true outcome mean (e.g., >1.5% gap over 10+ days), apply mean reversion bias: add 0.1–0.3x the historical volatility to forecast to align with recent trend.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive (e.g., +0.3+ in 3 days), model often lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.2–0.5x the sentiment magnitude to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently underpredicts in early days (days 1–7) and overpredicts in late days (days 24–30), apply “early under, late over” correction: add 0.3–0.6% to early days and subtract 0.2–0.5% from late days to smooth out bias.
